# Ansible variables

Set per machine in `ansible/inventory/host_vars/<machine>.yml` (start from the commented `example-machine.yml`); secrets go into the Ansible Vault file `ansible/group_vars/all/vault.yml`. Lab-wide defaults live in `ansible/group_vars/all/main.yml`; role variables are defined by each role's `meta/argument_specs.yml`, which Ansible also uses to validate them. Host facts such as `pinka_family` are not variables: the `platform_facts` role derives them from the host profile.

## Lab-wide variables

### `machine_name`

Host name of the machine in the tailnet, in /etc/wsl.conf and in the fingerprint.

- Default: `pinka-lab`

### `lab_mode`

production, or staging for QA environments (own vault, Tailscale tag and signing key; never pairs with a production host).

- Default: `production`

### `staging_shared_hardware`

Staging only: this staging host runs on production's hardware, so it starts only inside an open maintenance window with the GPU idle and its ports free (BUILD_PROMPT §7.20, pinka window open).

- Default: `false`

### `lab_provider`

Provider role: auto (the provider preflight detected), baremetal, wsl2 or vm. Any other value than auto must match the detected provider.

- Default: `auto`

### `power_policy`

Power policy on bare metal and VMs: never_sleep (sleep targets masked), lab_session_inhibit (a sleep inhibitor while pinka-lab.target is up) or os_default.

- Default: `lab_session_inhibit`

### `node_role`

What this host runs: full (everything), lab (everything except vLLM) or inference (only the inference stack).

- Default: `full`

### `inference`

The inference switch (BUILD_PROMPT §2.3): auto (vLLM, its images and the selected model where preflight detects gpu_inference on a full or inference node) or off (none of them is installed or counted in the requirements). An inference node needs auto.

- Default: `auto`

### `training`

The training switch (§2.3, §7.18), on a full node only: auto (training jobs where preflight detects gpu_training), cpu (also without a usable GPU: the jobs' CPU-only variant) or off (the GPU arbiter refuses every run, no job image is pulled, nothing is counted in the requirements).

- Default: `auto`

### `firewall_backend`

Firewall backend: auto (firewalld if active, else ufw if active, else nftables), nftables, firewalld or ufw.

- Default: `auto`

### `install_nvidia_driver`

NVIDIA driver: auto (install with the family's method), manual (the operator installs it) or skip. Ignored on WSL2, where the driver comes from Windows.

- Default: `auto`

### `allow_community_repos`

Allow community repositories (COPR, OBS home projects, RPM Fusion); recorded in the fingerprint. bootstrap.sh --allow-community-repos does the same.

- Default: `false`

### `gpu_arbiter`

The GPU arbiter (BUILD_PROMPT §7.18, §8.1): after_boot serve (the default deployment) or idle; restore_after_training brings the deployment served before a training run back when the run ends, unless the submission says otherwise.

- Default: `{after_boot: serve, restore_after_training: true}`

### `training_caps`

Infra's caps on training (§7.18): a job's run time, memory and CPUs (the arbiter refuses a run whose job exceeds them; validation and doctor warn), the size of a published dataset (dataset_max), the combined size of a run's output and checkpoints (run_storage_max: the free space a run needs to start, and the run is stopped and failed beyond it) and the job's /tmp (tmp_max: a tmpfs, counted against the job's memory). memory_max: auto computes the cap from the host (§2.3): MemTotal minus the recommended memory of the core stack and the targets, in whole GiB within 4 and 24 GiB (preflight records it in the host profile); a size such as 12G sets it.

- Default:

    ```yaml
    {timeout_seconds: 86400, memory_max: auto, cpus: 8, dataset_max: 8G, run_storage_max: 16G,
      tmp_max: 1G}
    ```

### `grafana_tailscale_serve`

Publish Grafana to the tailnet with `tailscale serve` (never Funnel).

- Default: `false`

### `docs_release`

The documentation release the docs service serves (BUILD_PROMPT §7.19): {url, sha256} of a release's documentation tarball (an https:// URL or an absolute path); null: no docs service.

- Default: `null`

### `docs_tailscale_serve`

Publish the docs service to the tailnet with `tailscale serve` (never Funnel).

- Default: `false`

### `tailscale_serve_consent`

On a Tailscale node that existed before pinka (adopted, BUILD_PROMPT §7.4): the owner's consent to publish Grafana or the docs with tailscale serve.

- Default: `false`

### `pinka_tailscale_serve_allowed`

Whether pinka may publish with tailscale serve at all: always on a node it joined, only with tailscale_serve_consent on an adopted node (§7.4).

- Default:

    ```jinja
    {{ (host_profile.components.tailscale | default({})).origin | default(none) != 'pre-existing'
       or tailscale_serve_consent | bool }}
    ```

### `ssh_extra_allowed_interfaces`

Interfaces besides tailscale0 on which sshd accepts connections.

- Default: `[]`

### `firewall_close_listeners`

Shared host: pre-existing listeners to close, as protocol/port such as [tcp/8080] (BUILD_PROMPT §2.2, §7.5); every other one stays reachable as preflight found it. The installer's Remote access screen sets it.

- Default: `[]`

### `firewall_close_install_path`

Close the install's access path (for example SSH from the LAN) once SSH over the tailnet was verified for a researcher in the same run (§7.5); without both it stays open and doctor warns.

- Default: `false`

### `pinka_root`

Root of the research space (BUILD_PROMPT §6.2).

- Default: `/srv/pinka`

### `cpuset_services`

CPUs of the lab services (Linux cpuset list such as "0-5"); empty: no pinning. Set per machine in host_vars; must not overlap cpuset_targets.

- Default: `''`

### `cpuset_targets`

CPUs of the Incus benchmark targets; empty: no pinning. The platform pins targets inside it (endpoints.toml), and it sizes the bench project's CPUs.

- Default: `''`

### `pinka_services_slice`

Systemd slice of every lab service and container (AllowedCPUs=cpuset_services).

- Default: `pinka-services.slice`

### `pinka_container_log_max_size`

Size limit of one log file of the `local` log driver of every lab container (Docker's own default), set per container by the Compose projects and the GPU arbiter rather than in the Docker daemon (BUILD_PROMPT §7.6).

- Default: `20m`

### `pinka_container_log_max_file`

Number of log files the `local` log driver keeps per lab container (Docker's own default), set like pinka_container_log_max_size.

- Default: `5`

### `allow_kernel_updates`

Let automatic security updates update the kernel on bare metal (held by default).

- Default: `false`

### `pinka_tailscale_tags`

Tailscale tag of the host per lab_mode (owner answer E2).

- Default: `{production: 'tag:pinka-lab', staging: 'tag:pinka-qa'}`

### `pinka_groups`

Groups created by users_groups.

- Default:

    ```yaml
    - {name: pinka, system: false, description: all researchers}
    - {name: pinka-admin, system: false, description: researchers with sudo}
    - {name: pinka-restricted, system: true, description: "restricted data: only accounts of restricted-capable\
        \ profiles (\xA712.4)"}
    - {name: pinka-datasets, system: true, description: "published training datasets: no human\
        \ members (\xA77.18)"}
    - {name: pinka-query, system: true, description: "the telemetry query proxy: exactly the accounts\
        \ of the profiles that query (\xA77.9)"}
    ```

### `researchers`

Placeholders (owner answer E1). keys_file is relative to the repository root; key files are never committed (users/*.pub is excluded by .gitignore). Optional per researcher: display_name (Grafana) and grafana: false (no Grafana account). The installer TUI edits this list.

- Default:

    ```yaml
    - {name: researcher1, admin: true, shell: /bin/bash, keys_file: users/researcher1.pub}
    - {name: researcher2, admin: false, shell: /bin/bash, keys_file: users/researcher2.pub}
    - {name: researcher3, admin: false, shell: /bin/bash, keys_file: users/researcher3.pub}
    ```

### `researchers_removed`

Researchers that left: locked (usermod -L, nologin), never deleted; data kept.

- Default: `[]`

### `break_glass_docker`

Admins that are explicitly allowed into the docker group (logged loudly).

- Default: `[]`

### `infra_accounts`

Infra's own system accounts (BUILD_PROMPT §6.1): no login, no password, no SSH keys. pinka-build runs platform builds in their sandbox (§7.14 step 5); pinka-inference runs the inference control endpoint of an inference node (§19.10) and holds its mutual-TLS key.

- Default:

    ```yaml
    - name: pinka-build
      groups: []
      description: unprivileged platform builds
    - name: pinka-inference
      groups: []
      description: the inference control endpoint of an inference node
    - name: pinka-query-proxy
      groups: []
      description: "the telemetry query proxy's container user (\xA77.9)"
    - name: pinka-otelcol
      groups: []
      description: "the gateway collector's container user (\xA77.9)"
    - name: pinka-prometheus
      groups: []
      description: "Prometheus's container user (\xA77.9)"
    - name: pinka-loki
      groups: []
      description: "Loki's container user (\xA77.9)"
    - name: pinka-tempo
      groups: []
      description: "Tempo's container user (\xA77.9)"
    - name: pinka-grafana
      groups: []
      description: "Grafana's container user (\xA77.9)"
    ```

### `inference_control_account`

The account of the inference control endpoint.

- Default: `pinka-inference`

### `pinka_platform_uids`

The platform's accounts and groups are not listed here: the platform role renders them from the active platform's manifest and profiles (§6.1, §12.2). Their UIDs come from this range (ADR-0016): systemd's table of UID and GID allocations (v255) lists it as unused; the deployment tool never takes a UID that is already in use.

- Default: `{min: 60578, max: 61183}`

### `pinka_telemetry_clients`

The only accounts that reach the telemetry stores directly (§7.9, ADR-0016 as decided with the "commit" for 3d.4 and 3d.4b): infra's own clients, each by name. The telemetry guard resets every other account's connection to the stores' ports on the host loopback: researchers, Grafana, the platform's services and everyone else query through the read-only query proxy and send through the collector's OTLP receivers. The guard matches UIDs only, never groups.

- Default:

    ```yaml
    - {account: root, reason: 'doctor, the health gate and administrators (sudo)'}
    - {account: pinka-otelcol, reason: the gateway collector writes to Loki and Tempo}
    - {account: pinka-prometheus, reason: 'Prometheus scrapes the collector, Loki, Tempo and itself'}
    - {account: pinka-loki, reason: Loki's own gRPC port}
    - {account: pinka-tempo, reason: Tempo's own gRPC and OTLP ports}
    - {account: pinka-query-proxy, reason: 'the query proxy, which forwards the query endpoints'}
    ```

### `pinka_query_port_clients`

The only accounts that reach the query proxy's loopback port: Grafana, whose data sources all go through the proxy (so no Grafana user, editor or admin included, reaches a push, admin or delete endpoint), and root. The platform's services that query use the proxy's socket and its group.

- Default:

    ```yaml
    - {account: root, reason: doctor and administrators (sudo)}
    - {account: pinka-grafana, reason: 'Grafana''s Prometheus, Loki and Tempo data sources'}
    ```

### `pinka_telemetry_guard_ports`

The stores' ports the telemetry guard closes to every other account (§7.9): Prometheus, Loki and Tempo (HTTP and gRPC, Tempo's OTLP receiver) and the collector's metrics exporter. The collector's OTLP receivers stay open.

- Default:

    ```jinja
    {{ [pinka_ports.prometheus, pinka_ports.loki, pinka_ports.tempo,
        pinka_internal_ports.loki_grpc, pinka_internal_ports.tempo_grpc,
        pinka_internal_ports.tempo_otlp_grpc, pinka_internal_ports.collector_metrics] | sort }}
    ```

### `pinka_inference_clients`

Infra's own clients of the inference API on the host loopback (BUILD_PROMPT §7.11, ADR-0016), per node role: the inference guard adds the active platform's accounts whose profile reaches the API (controller, inference broker) and resets every other account's connection to vLLM, or to the inference forwarder of a lab node. UIDs only, never groups.

- Default:

    ```yaml
    - account: root
      reason: doctor, the health gate, the serving verification and the GPU arbiter; vLLM's own
        health check
      node_roles: [full, lab, inference]
    - account: pinka-prometheus
      reason: Prometheus scrapes vLLM's metrics
      node_roles: [full]
    - account: pinka-otelcol
      reason: the collector scrapes vLLM's metrics
      node_roles: [full, inference]
    - account: pinka-inference
      reason: the control endpoint forwards the API
      node_roles: [inference]
    ```

### `pinka_service_home`

Parent of the infra and platform account homes (/var/lib/pinka/&lt;account&gt;).

- Default: `/var/lib/pinka`

### `pinka_python`

Pinned CPython installed by bootstrap (BUILD_PROMPT §19.3).

- Default: `/opt/pinka/python/bin/python3`

### `pinka_layout`

The research space layout, the single source of truth: the layout role creates exactly these entries, and tools/gen renders them into docs/architecture.md. `path` is relative to pinka_root ("" is pinka_root itself).

- Default:

    ```yaml
    - {path: '', owner: root, group: pinka, mode: '2775', notes: research space root}
    - {path: platforms, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0755', notes: 'per platform: releases/<ref>/,
        content/<package>/<ref>/, state/'}
    - {path: restricted, owner: root, group: pinka-restricted, mode: '0750', notes: 'restricted
        data per platform, files 0640'}
    - {path: models, owner: root, group: pinka, mode: '0755', notes: 'model weights, 0444 after
        verification'}
    - {path: models/adapters, owner: root, group: pinka, mode: '0755', notes: 'registered adapters,
        read-only, with lineage'}
    - {path: training, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0755', notes: parent of the training areas}
    - {path: training/datasets, owner: root, group: pinka-datasets, mode: '0750', notes: 'published
        training datasets, files 0640, each with PROVENANCE.json'}
    - {path: training/jobs, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0755', notes: 'per job run: output/
        and checkpoints/, owned by the job''s account'}
    - path: datasets
      owner: root
      group: pinka
      mode: '2775'
      default_acl: ['group:pinka:rwX']
      notes: shared datasets
    - {path: images, owner: root, group: pinka-admin, mode: '0750', notes: exported golden image
        tarballs with sha256}
    - path: shared
      owner: root
      group: pinka
      mode: '2770'
      default_acl: ['group:pinka:rwX']
      notes: shared files
    - {path: users, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0755', notes: parent of the per-researcher
        directories}
    - {path: services, owner: root, group: pinka-admin, mode: '0750', notes: 'rendered compose
        and config, never plaintext secrets readable by all'}
    - {path: state, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0755', notes: 'parent of state/<service>/
        (container UID, 0700), created by the service roles'}
    - {path: backups, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0700', notes: local backup staging only}
    ```

### `pinka_layout_user_mode`

Per-researcher directory: users/&lt;name&gt;/ owned by &lt;name&gt;:&lt;name&gt;, mode 0700.

- Default: `0700`

### `pinka_system_layout`

Host paths outside pinka_root (absolute).

- Default:

    ```yaml
    - {path: /etc/pinka, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0755', notes: 'host profile, bootstrap
        state, rendered non-secret config'}
    - {path: /etc/pinka/secrets, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0711', notes: 'rendered secrets,
        one directory per platform account (0750 root:<account>)'}
    - {path: /var/lib/pinka, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0755', notes: service homes and
        lab state}
    - {path: /etc/pinka/platform, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0755', notes: 'the active platform:
        active.json, principals.json, endpoints.toml'}
    - {path: /var/lib/pinka/git, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0700', notes: root-only Git
        mirrors of the platform and content sources}
    - {path: /var/lib/pinka/staging, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0700', notes: root-only
        run directories of deployments}
    - {path: /var/lib/pinka/platforms, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0700', notes: deployment
        and retirement records per platform}
    - {path: /var/cache/pinka, owner: root, group: root, mode: '0755', notes: caches}
    - {path: /var/cache/pinka/uv, owner: pinka-build, group: pinka-build, mode: '0700', notes: uv
        cache of the platform builds}
    ```

### `pinka_default_ports`

Default listener ports of the lab services (contracts.md#ports, BUILD_PROMPT §12.11). Override them per machine with `ports:`; read the effective values from pinka_ports.

- Default:

    ```yaml
    {otlp_grpc: 4317, otlp_http: 4318, opa: 8181, incus_https: 8443, grafana: 18700, prometheus: 18701,
      loki: 18702, tempo: 18703, vllm: 18704, gateway_adhoc: 18705, docs_serve: 18706, inference_control: 18710}
    ```

### `ports`

Port overrides by the names of pinka_default_ports, set in host_vars, for example {grafana: 18750}. Preflight reports a configured port that a process outside the lab uses; endpoints.toml carries the effective values.

- Default: `{}`

### `pinka_ports`

The effective listener ports: the defaults with the machine's overrides.

- Default: `{{ pinka_default_ports | combine(ports) }}`

### `pinka_preflight_args`

The preflight options of the machine's port overrides, VM collector address and pool device (bootstrap passes the same; the preflight gate and doctor re-run preflight with them).

- Default:

    ```jinja
    {{ (ports.items() | map('join', '=') | map('regex_replace', '^', '--port=') | list)
       + ['--vm-collector-address', vm_collector_address]
       + (['--pool-device', incus_pool_device]
          if incus_pool_source | default('loop') == 'device' and incus_pool_device | default('') | length > 0
          else []) }}
    ```

### `pinka_internal_ports`

Loopback ports of lab-internal listeners: exporters, the collectors' own metrics and health checks, Loki's and Tempo's internal servers. Not part of the contract; every observability container uses the host network and binds 127.0.0.1 (BUILD_PROMPT §7.9).

- Default:

    ```yaml
    {collector_metrics: 18720, collector_telemetry: 18721, journald_telemetry: 18722, node_exporter: 18723,
      cadvisor: 18724, postgres_exporter: 18725, gpu_exporter: 18726, tempo_otlp_grpc: 18727,
      loki_grpc: 18728, tempo_grpc: 18729, collector_health: 18730, journald_health: 18731, otlp_agent: 18732,
      query_proxy: 18733}
    ```

### `vm_collector_address`

Address of the collector listener for VM targets (BUILD_PROMPT §12.11) on the dummy interface of pinka_vm_otlp. Preflight reports it when it is already assigned or routed on the host, or overlaps the Docker pools, an Incus network or the tailnet range; choose another one in host_vars.

- Default: `198.18.0.1`

### `pinka_vm_otlp`

Dedicated collector listener for VM targets (contracts.md#telemetry, C4): an address on a dummy interface, reachable only from run networks through the run ACL and the firewall, OTLP gRPC and HTTP on the ports of pinka_ports. Set up only with the vm_targets feature.

- Default: `{interface: pinka-otlp0, address: '{{ vm_collector_address }}'}`

### `pinka_incus_bridge_patterns`

Incus bridges the firewall treats as Incus networks (contracts.md: run networks are named r-&lt;short&gt;; image builds use pinka-build0).

- Default: `[r-*, pinka-build0]`

### `pinka_incus_personal_bridge_patterns`

Bridges of the researchers' personal Incus projects (incusbr-&lt;uid&gt;); unlike run networks they have NAT and an uplink.

- Default: `[incusbr-*]`

### `platform`

The platform release to deploy: {repo, ref, path, tag_prefix}; empty: no platform. repo is an SSH URL (read-only deploy key generated on the host), an anonymous HTTPS URL or a root-owned file:/// repository, never a URL with credentials; ref a tag (recommended), branch or full commit; path the release's subdirectory ("" for the repository root); tag_prefix the prefix of its release tags.

- Default: `{}`

### `content`

Content packages of the platform's manifest: {&lt;package&gt;: {repo, ref, path, tag_prefix}}. A package from the release's repository must not overlap the release path or another package.

- Default: `{}`

### `pinka_source_known_hosts`

Extra known_hosts lines for SSH sources (GitHub's keys come from versions.lock.yml).

- Default: `[]`

### `require_signed_tags`

Deploy only tags carrying a valid SSH signature of an allowed signer (owner answer E16).

- Default: `false`

### `pinka_allowed_signers`

Allowed signers for signed tags, ssh-keygen allowed_signers lines ("&lt;principal&gt; &lt;key type&gt; &lt;key&gt;").

- Default: `[]`

### `inference_remote_node`

Tailnet name of the paired inference node of a lab node (node_role: lab, BUILD_PROMPT §19.10); set when the nodes are paired.

- Default: `''`

### `inference_lab_node`

Tailnet name of the paired lab node of an inference node (node_role: inference), which receives its telemetry; set when the nodes are paired.

- Default: `''`

### `qa_trusted_keys`

QA public keys trusted for attestations (BUILD_PROMPT §13.10): a list of {name: &lt;file name without .pem&gt;, pem: &lt;PEM public key&gt;}.

- Default: `[]`

## active_platform

Read what infra rendered for the active platform.

Entry points: `main` (Read what infra rendered for the active platform). Role README: `ansible/roles/active_platform/README.md`.

### `active_platform_file`

The rendering of the active platform (infra-internal, no secrets).

- Type: `path`
- Default: `/etc/pinka/platform/rendered.json`

## backup

restic backups of pinka_root and /etc/pinka, PostgreSQL dumps, retention and backup metrics.

Entry points: `main` (restic backups of pinka_root and /etc/pinka, PostgreSQL dumps, retention and backup metrics). Role README: `ansible/roles/backup/README.md`.

Variables the role reads from elsewhere:

| Variable | Set by | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `machine_name` | [lab-wide](#machine_name) | Host name recorded in the snapshots; prune and restore select this host's snapshots. |
| `node_role` | [lab-wide](#node_role) | PostgreSQL is dumped on full and lab nodes. |
| `pinka_root` | [lab-wide](#pinka_root) | Research space root; its directories of backup_include are backed up. |
| `pinka_versions` | host_vars | The pinned versions (the restic binary). |

### `backup_repository`

restic repository (default vault_restic_repository); empty means backups are not configured.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `{{ vault_restic_repository | default('') }}`

### `backup_password`

Repository password (default vault_restic_password); written once, changed by rotate.yml.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `{{ vault_restic_password | default('') }}`

### `backup_sftp_known_hosts`

known_hosts lines of the SFTP backup server, required for an sftp repository.

- Type: `list` of `str`
- Default: `[]`

### `backup_include`

Infra's own directories below pinka_root that are backed up; the restricted area, the training datasets, the adapters and the platform's backup.paths always are.

- Type: `list` of `str`
- Default: `[images, datasets, shared, users, backups/pg]`

### `backup_include_models`

Also back up the model weights (re-downloaded and verified on restore otherwise).

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `false`

### `backup_include_state`

Directories of pinka_root/state to back up as well (prometheus, loki, tempo).

- Type: `list` of `str`
- Default: `[]`

### `backup_include_secrets`

Also back up the secret material under /etc/pinka (needs backup_secrets_acknowledged).

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `false`

### `backup_secrets_acknowledged`

Confirms that only the repository's encryption protects backed-up secrets.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `false`

### `backup_pgdump_keep`

Local PostgreSQL dumps kept.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `7`

### `backup_pgdump_schedule`

OnCalendar of the PostgreSQL dump.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `*-*-* 02:30:00`

### `backup_schedule`

OnCalendar of the restic backup.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `*-*-* 03:00:00`

### `backup_prune_schedule`

OnCalendar of the retention and prune job.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `Sun *-*-* 04:00:00`

### `backup_retention`

Snapshots kept by the prune job (keep-daily, keep-weekly, keep-monthly).

- Type: `dict`
- Default: `{daily: 7, weekly: 4, monthly: 12}`

## base

Base system.

Entry points: `main` (Base system). Role README: `ansible/roles/base/README.md`.

Variables the role reads from elsewhere:

| Variable | Set by | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allow_kernel_updates` | [lab-wide](#allow_kernel_updates) | On bare metal, let automatic updates install kernels (default false). |

### `base_packages`

Logical package names, mapped per family in vars/&lt;family&gt;.yml.

- Type: `list` of `str`
- Default:

    ```yaml
    [ca_certificates, curl, gpg, jq, git, acl, btrfs_tools, lvm2, thin_provisioning_tools, nftables,
      rsync, tmux, htop, iotop, sysstat, sudo, xz, zstd, bzip2, tar, python_debian]
    ```

### `base_journald_system_max_use`

journald SystemMaxUse.

### `base_journald_system_keep_free`

journald SystemKeepFree.

### `base_auto_updates`

Automatic security updates on fixed releases (never on rolling releases).

### `base_auto_updates_effective`

Derived; base_auto_updates and not a rolling release.

### `base_held_package_patterns`

Packages automatic updates never touch (pinned by pinka).

### `base_hold_kernel`

Derived; hold the kernel (bare metal unless allow_kernel_updates).

### `base_kernel_package_patterns`

Kernel package patterns for apt.

- Type: `list` of `str`
- Default: `[linux-image-, linux-headers-, linux-modules-]`

### `base_kernel_package_patterns_rpm`

Kernel package patterns for dnf.

- Type: `list` of `str`
- Default: `[kernel*]`

### `base_sysctl`

Kernel settings in /etc/sysctl.d/60-pinka.conf.

- Type: `dict`
- Default:

## doctor

The pinka operator CLI, a copy of preflight it runs, and the lab description /etc/pinka/lab.json.

Entry points: `main` (The pinka operator CLI, a copy of preflight it runs, and the lab description /etc/pinka/lab.json). Role README: `ansible/roles/doctor/README.md`.

Variables the role reads from elsewhere:

| Variable | Set by | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `host_profile` | bootstrap.sh | The validated host profile (storage backend of the Incus pool). |
| `machine` | bootstrap.sh | Name of the host_vars file (bootstrap --machine); pinka passes it back to bootstrap. |
| `machine_name` | [lab-wide](#machine_name) | Machine name; the Tailscale host name doctor expects. |
| `node_role` | [lab-wide](#node_role) | full, lab or inference; selects the units, containers and Incus, PostgreSQL and image checks. |
| `pinka_dir` | host_vars | Infra directory of the checkout bootstrap runs from; the sources of the CLI and the blueprints. |
| `pinka_features` | host_vars | Feature flags after the switches (gpu_inference, gpu_training, vm_targets; preflight_gate). |
| `pinka_provider` | host_vars | Provider of this host (WSL checks, sleep inhibitor, nvidia-smi path). |
| `pinka_training` | host_vars | Where training jobs run (preflight_gate); lab.json tells the CLI whether this host trains. |
| `pinka_training_caps` | host_vars | The training caps with memory_max auto replaced by the computed cap (preflight_gate); in lab.json. |
| `pinka_versions` | host_vars | The pinned versions (the image and digest every lab container must run). |

### `doctor_max_clock_offset`

Largest clock offset doctor accepts, in seconds.

- Type: `float`
- Default: `1.0`

### `doctor_min_pool_free_gib`

Free space of the Incus pool below which doctor warns, in GiB.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `20`

### `doctor_disk_warn_free_percent`

Free share of a mount point the lab uses below which doctor warns.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `15`

### `doctor_disk_full_within_days`

Doctor warns when the trend of its recorded runs fills a mount point within these days.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `7`

### `doctor_backup_max_age_hours`

Age of the last successful backup after which doctor warns, in hours.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `26`

### `doctor_telemetry_wait`

Seconds doctor waits for its telemetry probe to arrive in Loki, Tempo and Prometheus.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `60`

### `doctor_smoke_wait`

Seconds doctor --smoke waits for a throwaway target's logs in Loki.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `120`

### `doctor_certificate_renew_days`

Days before a pairing certificate expires at which doctor fails inference.pairing.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `30`

### `doctor_drain_timeout`

Seconds `pinka stop` and `update-host` give the platform's drain hook.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `1800`

### `doctor_health_wait`

Seconds `pinka start` waits for the platform's health hook to answer ok.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `300`

### `doctor_listener_processes`

Processes that may listen outside loopback (names as `ss -p` shows them).

- Type: `list` of `str`
- Default: `[sshd, tailscaled, dnsmasq, systemd-network, dhclient, NetworkManager, chronyd]`

## firewall

Firewall policy with the nftables, firewalld or ufw backend.

Entry points: `main` (Firewall policy with the nftables, firewalld or ufw backend). Role README: `ansible/roles/firewall/README.md`.

Variables the role reads from elsewhere:

| Variable | Set by | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `grafana_tailscale_serve` | [lab-wide](#grafana_tailscale_serve) | Open the Grafana serve port on the tailnet interface. |
| `inference_remote_node` | [lab-wide](#inference_remote_node) | The paired inference node of a lab node; its telemetry arrives on OTLP gRPC. |
| `node_role` | [lab-wide](#node_role) | Inference nodes and paired lab nodes open the split-inference ports. |
| `pinka_incus_bridge_patterns` | [lab-wide](#pinka_incus_bridge_patterns) | Interface name patterns of Incus bridges (run networks and the build bridge). |
| `pinka_incus_personal_bridge_patterns` | [lab-wide](#pinka_incus_personal_bridge_patterns) | Interface name patterns of the bridges of personal Incus projects. |
| `pinka_ports` | [lab-wide](#pinka_ports) | Contract ports (vllm, inference_control, otlp_grpc). |
| `pinka_vm_otlp` | [lab-wide](#pinka_vm_otlp) | Interface and address of the collector listener for VM targets (C4). |
| `ssh_extra_allowed_interfaces` | [lab-wide](#ssh_extra_allowed_interfaces) | Interfaces besides tailscale0 on which SSH is reachable. |

### `firewall_close_listeners`

Shared host, pre-existing listeners to close with the owner's consent (tcp/8080 and the like).

- Type: `list` of `str`
- Required, no default

### `firewall_close_install_path`

Close the install's access path once SSH over the tailnet is verified in the same run.

- Type: `bool`
- Required, no default

### `firewall_tailnet_interface`

Tailnet interface.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `tailscale0`

### `firewall_grafana_serve_port`

TCP port of `tailscale serve` for Grafana.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `443`

### `firewall_docs_serve_port`

TCP port of `tailscale serve` for the docs service.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `10000`

### `firewall_tailnet_tcp_ports`

TCP ports open on the tailnet interface (derived: 22, the serve port if enabled, 18704 and 18710 on an inference node, 4317 on a paired lab node).

- Type: `list` of `int`
- Default:

    ```jinja
    {{ [22]
       + ([firewall_grafana_serve_port] if grafana_tailscale_serve | bool and pinka_tailscale_serve_allowed | bool else [])
       + ([firewall_docs_serve_port]
          if docs_tailscale_serve | bool and docs_release is not none and pinka_tailscale_serve_allowed | bool else [])
       + ([pinka_ports.vllm, pinka_ports.inference_control] if node_role == 'inference' else [])
       + ([pinka_ports.otlp_grpc] if node_role == 'lab' and inference_remote_node | length > 0 else []) }}
    ```

### `firewall_tailscale_udp_port`

UDP port of the WireGuard transport of tailscaled.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `41641`

### `firewall_run_bridge_pattern`

Name pattern of the per-run networks; nothing is forwarded out of them.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `r-*`

### `firewall_vm_otlp_ports`

OTLP ports VM targets may reach on the listener address (derived; empty without vm_targets).

- Type: `list` of `int`
- Default:

    ```jinja
    {{ [pinka_ports.otlp_grpc, pinka_ports.otlp_http]
       if (pinka_features.vm_targets | default(false)) and node_role in ['full', 'lab'] else [] }}
    ```

### `firewall_incus_bridge_patterns`

Every Incus bridge that may use DHCP and DNS on the host (derived).

- Type: `list` of `str`
- Default: `{{ pinka_incus_bridge_patterns + pinka_incus_personal_bridge_patterns }}`

### `firewall_uplink_bridge_patterns`

Incus bridges with NAT and an uplink, trusted as Incus documents (derived).

- Type: `list` of `str`
- Default: `{{ ['pinka-build0'] + pinka_incus_personal_bridge_patterns }}`

### `firewall_preexisting_bridges`

Bridges of a pre-existing LXD, on which the input policy admits DHCP and DNS for LXD's dnsmasq (derived from the host profile).

- Type: `list` of `str`
- Default:

    ```jinja
    {{ (((host_profile | default({})).components | default({})).lxd | default({})).networks | default([])
       | map(attribute='name') | select('match', '^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,15}$') | list }}
    ```

### `firewall_access`

The access to the host before pinka's first install, from the install record (derived; empty for a legacy record).

- Type: `dict`
- Default: `{{ (pinka_preexisting | default({})).access | default({}) }}`

### `firewall_listener_rules`

The pre-existing listeners kept and closed, and those held open for the install's access path (derived, pinka_listener_rules).

- Type: `dict`
- Default: `{{ firewall_access | pinka_listener_rules(firewall_close_listeners, pinka_closed_access | default([])) }}`

### `firewall_install_path`

The install's access path while it is pinka's to keep (address, port, family, user, closed), or none (derived, pinka_install_path).

- Type: `raw`
- Default: `{{ firewall_access | pinka_install_path(pinka_closed_access | default([])) }}`

Root of the exports, &lt;blueprint&gt;/&lt;version&gt;/ and _upstream/&lt;base&gt;/&lt;fingerprint&gt;/ (pinka_root/images).

Python regular expressions that fail the build when the build adds a match.


Benign words ({match, optional path}, regular expressions) cut out of a finding before the patterns are applied again.

- Type: `list` of `dict`

## incus

Incus LTS with the pool, networks, run ACL, projects, profiles and service certificates.

Entry points: `main` (Incus LTS with the pool, networks, run ACL, projects, profiles and service certificates). Role README: `ansible/roles/incus/README.md`.

Variables the role reads from elsewhere:

| Variable | Set by | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `host_profile` | bootstrap.sh | Host profile (storage_backend, hardware, requirements.pool) passed by bootstrap. |
| `pinka_bootstrap` | bootstrap.sh | Bootstrap options (adopt_incus, interactive). |
| `pinka_dir` | host_vars | Infra directory of the checkout (incus/ templates). |
| `pinka_vm_otlp` | [lab-wide](#pinka_vm_otlp) | Interface and address of the collector listener for VM targets (C4). |
| `researchers` | [lab-wide](#researchers) | Researchers; each gets a personal project and joins the Incus user group. |

### `incus_pool_name`

Storage pool of all instances.

- Type: `str`

### `incus_pool_source`

A loop file in the root filesystem, or a dedicated device.

- Type: `str`

- Default: `loop`

### `incus_pool_size`

Size of a loop pool, such as 300GiB, or auto: the size preflight computed from the golden images, the concurrent targets' root disks and the free space (host profile requirements.pool, BUILD_PROMPT §2.3). An existing pool keeps its size.

### `incus_pool_device`

Dedicated device for the pool (use /dev/disk/by-id/...).

Must repeat incus_pool_device exactly, or nothing is formatted.

Format the device even though it carries a filesystem, LVM or RAID signature.

- Type: `bool`

### `incus_https_address`

Address of the Incus HTTPS API (restricted TLS clients and metrics).

- Type: `str`

### `incus_build_network`

NAT bridge of the build project.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `pinka-build0`

### `incus_run_acl`

Network ACL the platform attaches to every run network.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `pinka-run-default`

### `incus_run_acl_egress`

Egress rules of the run ACL (derived; OTLP to the VM listener with vm_targets).

- Type: `list` of `dict`
- Default:

    ```jinja
    {{ [{'action': 'allow', 'state': 'enabled', 'protocol': 'tcp',
         'destination': pinka_vm_otlp.address ~ '/32',
         'destination_port': pinka_ports.otlp_grpc ~ ',' ~ pinka_ports.otlp_http,
         'description': 'OTLP to the collector listener for VM targets'}]
       if pinka_features.vm_targets | default(false) else [] }}
    ```

### `incus_max_virtual_machines`

Most VMs at once in the bench and build projects (with the vm_targets feature).

- Type: `int`
- Default: `4`

### `incus_concurrent_targets`

Targets that run at once; they size the bench project's memory and the memory preflight requires.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `2`

### `incus_bench_limits`

Project limits of bench (memory from the concurrent targets, CPUs from cpuset_targets or the host's CPUs).

- Type: `dict`
- Default:

    ```yaml
    {limits.memory: "{{ (incus_concurrent_targets | int)\n   * (((incus_target_vm if pinka_features.vm_targets\
        \ | default(false) else incus_target_container).memory\n       | pinka_size_mib)\n   \
        \   + (incus_probe_client.memory | pinka_size_mib)) }}MiB", limits.cpu: "{{ (cpuset_targets\
        \ | pinka_cpuset_cpus | length) if cpuset_targets\n   else [(host_profile.hardware.cpu_threads_effective\
        \ | int) - 2, 1] | max }}", limits.instances: '40'}
    ```

### `incus_target_container`

Default limits and root disk of the target-container profile.

- Type: `dict`
- Default: `{cpu: '1', memory: 1GiB, root_size: 8GiB}`

### `incus_target_vm`

Default limits and root disk of the target-vm profile.

- Type: `dict`
- Default: `{cpu: '2', memory: 2GiB, root_size: 16GiB}`

### `incus_probe_client`

Limits and root disk of the probe-client profile.

- Type: `dict`
- Default: `{cpu: '1', memory: 512MiB, root_size: 4GiB}`

### `incus_build_instance`

Limits and root disk of the build profile.

- Type: `dict`
- Default: `{cpu: '2', memory: 2GiB, root_size: 16GiB}`

### `incus_user_limits`

Project limits of each personal project.

## platform

Deploy the platform release and its content packages (contract v2), if a platform source is set.

| `pinka_features` | host_vars | Feature flags (gpu_inference decides local inference). |
| `pinka_ports` | [lab-wide](#pinka_ports) | Effective ports (endpoints.toml, the inference broker's port). |
| `pinka_source_known_hosts` | [lab-wide](#pinka_source_known_hosts) | known_hosts lines for SSH sources other than GitHub. |
| `pinka_versions` | host_vars | The pinned versions (Quarto). |
| `pinka_vm_otlp` | [lab-wide](#pinka_vm_otlp) | The VM collector address (endpoints.toml). |

| `vault_platform_secrets` | host_vars | The secrets the manifest names, {&lt;service&gt;: {&lt;name&gt;: value}}. |

- Default:

    ```yaml
    update-initramfs: [update-initramfs, -u, -k, all]
    dracut: [dracut, --force, --regenerate-all]
    mkinitcpio: [mkinitcpio, -P]
    ```

### `provider_baremetal_mok_keys`

Certificates DKMS signs modules with; the first that exists is imported as a Machine Owner Key when Secure Boot is on and it is not enrolled.

- Type: `list` of `path`
- Default: `[/var/lib/shim-signed/mok/MOK.der, /var/lib/dkms/mok.pub]`

[interop] appendWindowsPath.

[network] generateHosts.

- Type: `bool`

### `provider_wsl2_generate_resolv_conf`

[network] generateResolvConf.

Distribution name in the restart instruction (from WSL_DISTRO_NAME when available).

## ssh

sshd drop-in with key-only login for the pinka group.

Entry points: `main` (sshd drop-in with key-only login for the pinka group). Role README: `ansible/roles/ssh/README.md`.

Variables the role reads from elsewhere:

| Variable | Set by | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `researchers` | [lab-wide](#researchers) | The researchers; an install session of another account keeps the host's policy until the safeguard closes its path. |

### `ssh_allow_groups`

Groups allowed to log in (AllowGroups).

- Type: `list` of `str`
- Default: `[pinka]`

### `ssh_client_alive_interval`

ClientAliveInterval in seconds.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `60`

### `ssh_server_package`

OpenSSH server package per family.

- Type: `dict`
- Default:

    ```yaml
    {debian: openssh-server, redhat: openssh-server, suse: openssh-server, archlinux: openssh}
    ```

### `ssh_access`

The access to the host before pinka's first install, from the install record (derived).

- Type: `dict`
- Default: `{{ (pinka_preexisting | default({})).access | default({}) }}`

### `ssh_install_path`

The install's access path while it is pinka's to keep, or none (derived, pinka_install_path).

- Type: `raw`
- Default: `{{ ssh_access | pinka_install_path(pinka_closed_access | default([])) }}`

### `ssh_policy_scope`

Where pinka's sshd settings apply, host or a Match Group block (shared host, or the install's path open for a non-researcher; derived).

- Type: `str`
- Choices: `host`, `group`
- Default:

    ```jinja
    {{ 'group' if ssh_access.host | default('dedicated') == 'shared'
       or (ssh_install_path is not none and not ssh_install_path.closed
           and ssh_install_path.user not in (researchers | map(attribute='name') | list))
       else 'host' }}
    ```

## tailscale

Install Tailscale, join the tailnet with the lab's tag, check that Funnel is off; a node logged in before pinka is adopted as it is.

Entry points: `main` (Install Tailscale, join the tailnet with the lab's tag, check that Funnel is off; a node logged in before pinka is adopted as it is). Role README: `ansible/roles/tailscale/README.md`.

Variables the role reads from elsewhere:

| Variable | Set by | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `grafana_tailscale_serve` | [lab-wide](#grafana_tailscale_serve) | Publish Grafana on the tailnet with `tailscale serve` (never Funnel). |
| `lab_mode` | [lab-wide](#lab_mode) | Selects the tag (tag:pinka-lab or tag:pinka-qa). |
| `machine_name` | [lab-wide](#machine_name) | Host name on the tailnet. |

### `tailscale_serve_consent`

On a node that existed before pinka, the owner's consent to tailscale serve for Grafana or docs.

- Type: `bool`

### `tailscale_tag`

Advertised tag; derived from lab_mode.

- Type: `str`
- Default: `{{ pinka_tailscale_tags[lab_mode] }}`

### `tailscale_accept_dns`

Let MagicDNS change host name resolution.

- Type: `bool`
- Default: `false`

### `tailscale_up_argv`

Arguments of `tailscale up` (without the auth key).

- Type: `list` of `str`
- Default:

    ```yaml
    [tailscale, up, '--hostname={{ machine_name }}', '--advertise-tags={{ tailscale_tag }}', '--accept-dns={{
        tailscale_accept_dns | bool | lower }}', --ssh=false]
    ```

### `tailscale_login_timeout`

Seconds to wait for an interactive login.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `600`

### `tailscale_grafana_serve_port`

HTTPS port of the Grafana serve.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `443`

### `tailscale_docs_serve_port`

HTTPS port of the docs service's serve.

- Type: `int`
- Default: `10000`
